task_instance: Write an ExtendScript (.jsx) that creates a new Illustrator document, draws a rounded-rectangle badge with a fill color, adds centered text on top, exports the result as a PNG, and saves the .ai file -- then run it in Adobe Illustrator to verify the actual PNG/AI deliverable.
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable is producing a working Illustrator automation result, which requires actually executing the .jsx script inside Adobe Illustrator's ExtendScript engine (via File > Scripts, the Scripts menu, or an external launcher driving the running application) to manipulate the DOM and produce a real .ai/.png artifact. Adobe Illustrator is a licensed, GUI-only desktop application available solely on Windows and macOS; this runtime is headless Linux with no GUI, no Windows/macOS environment, no Illustrator installation, and no ExtendScript interpreter, Wine, or Illustrator-compatible engine of any kind (verified: no `illustrator`, `osascript`, or `wine` binaries present, uname shows Linux). There is no package or dependency that can be installed to obtain Illustrator in this environment -- it is not merely absent from this sandbox but categorically outside what the described runtime (shell commands, dev tools, browser) can run. I could write syntactically correct, pattern-following ExtendScript source per the skill's guidance, but could not execute it against a real Illustrator DOM, so the actual deliverable (a rendered PNG/AI badge) could not be produced or verified.
